text:
alex: Early morning canary in eu-west-1 showing keystore decryption errors after we deployed tighter netpols + host egress ACLs. Keystore pods in namespace `keystore` log 'decrypt: no route to host' and we see NO KMS audit entries. Need triage and quick mitigation.

priya: I'm seeing the same in staging. Netpol is deny-by-default and we rolled an ipset-based ACL on nodes to limit egress to known CDNs. That likely blocked the KMS IP range. Can someone repro TCP connectivity from a pod?

gary: Repro commands and result:
```
kubectl -n keystore exec keystore-0 -- nc -vz kms-eu-west.kms.internal 443
nc: connect to kms-eu-west.kms.internal (10.10.200.45) port 443 (tcp) failed: Network is unreachable
```
No SYN reached KMS, so the KMS control plane never logs a request id for these attempts.

nina: Two things here: 1) connectivity (netpol/node ACL) is the immediate outage cause, 2) unrelatedly the canary image we used has openssl 1.1.1d flagged by SCA as a moderate CVE. We'll treat vulnerability as follow-up.

alex: Immediate mitigation options: (A) temporarily open egress to the KMS IP range in node ACLs + netpol, (B) deploy an egress-proxy sidecar (lightweight) for keystore to log outbound requests before network denial so we retain audit trail. Which can we do now?

priya: I can patch node ACLs and update the networkpolicy in ~12m. Proposed netpol patch (hotfix):
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-egress-kms
  namespace: keystore
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.10.200.0/24
      ports:
      - protocol: TCP
        port: 443
```
I'll coordinate with infra to bump the node ACLs too.

gary: I'll add an alert: if keystore decrypt error rate > 5% for 3m, page oncall. Also add a guard that flags if KMS audit shows missing request_ids for decrypts for >1m.

nina: For the CVE: I will build a patched keystore image (openssl 1.1.1u) and run a canary. If clean, schedule a patch window. Image scanning policy will be updated to block merges that modify the keystore deployment image without sec approval.

alex: Note on RBAC: recent PRs tightened the `svc-keystore` service account; while not the root cause here, we should avoid concurrent RBAC+netpol changes without explicit coordination. Proposal: require security sign-off on RBAC PRs touching critical svc accounts (e.g., svc-keystore). Thoughts?

priya: +1 on a merge gate or CODEOWNERS entry for RBAC touching private infra SAs.

incident-bot: incident created INC-2026-087 "keystore egress blocked by netpol+node-acl; missing KMS audit" severity=P2 responders=pagerduty/infra

alex: Recovery timeline: 12:15 UTC patch node ACLs, 12:22 UTC apply netpol update, 12:25 UTC restart keystore pods. After restart we observed decrypt success and KMS audit ids again. Example log: 
```
2026-08-03T12:26:01Z keystore INFO decrypt ok request_id=kms-eu-88abc
```

nina: Follow-ups (I'll open tickets):
1) Maintain an automated IPSet for KMS endpoints (owner: infra/priya).
2) Implement egress-proxy pattern with mandatory outbound logging for keystore so network-denied requests are visible (owner: platform/gary).
3) RBAC merge gate for serviceaccounts in private infra (owner: sec/alex).
4) Patch keystore image to remove CVE (owner: eng/nina).
5) Add netpol e2e test in staging to validate keystore->KMS path after any netpol push (owner: qa).

alex: Agreed. Operational note: keep deny-all-by-default, but maintain a small, automated allowlist for core infra (KMS, STS, metadata). All netpol/node-acl changes that affect keystore must be cross-checked against the allowlist and staged with a canary. Closing this thread after tickets are created and actions assigned. :white_check_mark:
